title: Clone Graph
description: DFS with a visited Map from original-node to clone-node. The Map handles cycles AND avoids exponential reclones of shared neighbors.

notes: CRITICAL: set map.set(orig, copy) BEFORE recursing into neighbors. Otherwise a cycle re-enters dfs and infinite-loops.
The Map keys are the original node OBJECTS (identity), not their .val — vals can repeat.
For each original node you create exactly one clone, then wire its neighbors by recursing or fetching from the map.

questions.q: Why must you put the clone in the map BEFORE recursing into neighbors?
options: Otherwise a cycle re-enters dfs on a node that is not yet recorded and recurses forever

questions.q: What are the keys of the visited Map?
For a null input, the function returns:

exercises.prompt: Fill in the DFS clone. The order of the two lines after creating copy is load-bearing.

blanks.hint: already cloned — return the stored copy

L3.prompt: Write `cloneGraph(node)` using DFS + a visited Map. Build the 4-cycle graph with edges 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 4-1, clone it, then log (1) `cloned !== original` (deep-copy proof), (2) a DFS-order serialization as `val:[n1,n2,...]` entries space-separated.
hints: Map original-node → clone-node, keyed by object identity.
Record the clone in the map BEFORE recursing into its neighbors, or a cycle infinite-loops.
For each neighbor, push dfs(neighbor) — dfs returns either the cached clone or a fresh one.
